noticias.titulo: Bienvenidos a la nueva Xataka
noticias.resumen: Hoy estamos de estreno: bienvenidos a la nueva Xataka. Durante años, Xataka ha sido más que una web. Ha sido un lugar para leer, sí, pero también para comentar, debatir, compartir y participar. La nueva Xataka bebe de esto y lo lleva un poco más allá para dar el mayor cambio que hemos hecho en años : no es sólo un cambio estético, es un cambio total en cómo contamos las cosas. 2027 es el año 1 de la nueva Xataka. Dejaremos de ser sólo una web que publica artículos para convertirnos en un lugar vivo. Un sitio donde una historia puede ser un análisis, un vídeo, un audio, una conversación en…
noticias.contenido: Hoy estamos de estreno: bienvenidos a la nueva Xataka. Durante años, Xataka ha sido más que una web. Ha sido un lugar para leer, sí, pero también para comentar, debatir, compartir y participar. La nueva Xataka bebe de esto y lo lleva un poco más allá para dar el mayor cambio que hemos hecho en años : no es sólo un cambio estético, es un cambio total en cómo contamos las cosas. 2027 es el año 1 de la nueva Xataka. Dejaremos de ser sólo una web que publica artículos para convertirnos en un lugar vivo. Un sitio donde una historia puede ser un análisis, un vídeo, un audio, una conversación en directo o una pieza breve que puedes consumir en un minuto. Porque a veces simplemente nos gustaría recomendarte algo que hemos encontrado y nos ha encantado, presentarte el último capítulo de nuestro podcast , hacer algo de humor con una caída de servicios a nivel global o nos apetece contar de una forma más original que GTA VI es toda una obra de ingeniería. De web a plataforma Todo empieza por la portada, que ha dejado de ser una lista de noticias para convertirse en un espacio donde pasan cosas (¡hasta pasatiempos !). Para cada historia elegiremos el mejor formato. Y detrás de todo siguen nuestros periodistas: no sólo como firmas de texto, sino como las caras y las voces de Xataka. Nos vais a ver mucho más. Una "vuelta a los orígenes" donde nuestro tono será mucho más personal y donde podréis conocer a fondo a todos los que hacemos Xataka. Pero la nueva Xataka también será más vuestra: podréis seguir a los periodistas y los temas que os interesen (o dejar de seguir a los que no). Podréis personalizar vuestra portada y, poco a poco, tener más control sobre lo que queréis ver. Y más cosas que irán llegando. Hoy damos el primer paso Hoy damos el primer paso hacia esta nueva Xataka con nuestra nueva portada . Es una primera versión, no incluye aún todas las funcionalidades que os hemos contado (y muchas otras que os iremos presentando y llegarán próximamente). Es sólo el comienzo. Pero es el comienzo de una nueva etapa que queremos construir con vosotros. ¿Cómo podéis ver todo lo que hemos preparado? Entrando directamente a xataka.com . Nos encantaría conocer vuestro feedback y sugerencias. Tenéis los comentarios y mi correo a vuestra disposición. ¡Gracias y os invitamos a vivir esta nueva etapa con nosotros! - La noticia Bienvenidos a la nueva Xataka fue publicada originalmente en Xataka por María González .

noticias.contenido: Cuando la lavadora acaba y se saca la ropa para tenderla, hay una pregunta que puede rondar muchas cabezas: ¿hay que dejar la puerta de la lavadora abierta para que 'respire' o es mejor cerrarla? Aquí podemos decir que hay dos filosofías muy diferentes, ya que hay gente que por estética o por el hecho de no tropezar cree firmemente que lo mejor es mantenerlo cerrado. Es un debate. Ante una pregunta que es bastante recurrente en el día a día, los fabricantes como Miele o Siemens se han pronunciado, al igual que también lo ha hecho la propia OCU . Y aquí la opinión es bastante unánime al apuntar que, tras sacar la ropa mojada, lo mejor es dejar tanto la puerta como el cajetín del detergente abiertos para que se seque todo el interior. El miedo. El principal freno para muchos usuarios es la presión a la que se someten las bisagras cuando la puerta se queda abierta durante mucho tiempo. Pero aquí los fabricantes apuntan a que estos componentes están preparados para soportar la carga de la puerta cuando está abierta sin ningún tipo de problema. Pero además de pensar en la puerta, los fabricantes también han tenido en cuenta la posibilidad de que alguien se apoye ligeramente sobre ella al cargar o descargar la ropa. Es por ello que dejarla abierta no supone ningún esfuerzo. En Xataka Xiaomi lanza en Europa una lavasecadora con tres tambores. En China es una costumbre, aquí de momento es una rareza En microbiología. Una vez tenemos en cuenta que la bisagra no va a sufrir por dejar la lavadora abierta, la pregunta que debemos hacernos es: ¿por qué? Aquí es donde entra el miedo de que aparezcan unos invitados indeseados en la lavadora, como son los hongos. Pero el problema aquí no es el tambor, que suele quedar prácticamente escurrido, sino que debemos fijarnos en la parte inferior de esa goma donde queda atrapada una pequeña piscina de agua residual mezclada con restos de detergente, suavizante, fibras y hasta grasa. Y es algo que tiene todo el sentido, porque si se cierra la puerta inmediatamente después del lavado, esa mezcla de agua y materia orgánica se evapora a un ritmo muy lento . Esto hace que los microorganismos tengan un auténtico paraíso para poder proliferar e ir pasando de colada en colada. Lo que vive. Cuando esa humedad se cronifica, la goma deja de ser un simple aislante para convertirse en un ecosistema complejo dominado por biopelículas, hongos y bacterias. En 2015, un estudio publicado en Fungal Biology analizó 70 lavadoras domésticas en Eslovenia y detectó hongos en el 79 % de ellas, destacando especies como las especies Fusarium , Exophiala o Candida parapsilosis , hongos oportunistas capaces de provocar infecciones en la piel, las uñas o los ojos en personas que estén inmunodeprimidas. Pero es algo que se ha seguido viendo, ya que un estudio publicado en 2023 elevó la presencia de hongos al 82% de las lavadoras analizadas, señalando los pliegues internos de la goma como el punto de mayor densidad de colonización. Además, un análisis comparativo publicado en Frontiers in Microbiology en 2025 observó que las lavadoras de carga frontal albergan una carga microbiana notablemente superior a las de carga superior, aunque puede existir algún sesgo de fondo. El olor. En el terreno bacteriano, el protagonista indiscutible del clásico olor a «trapo húmedo» en la ropa recién lavada tiene nombre propio desde que investigadores de la compañía japonesa Kao publicaron un estudio clave: Moraxella osloensis . Esta bacteria sobrevive bien al lavado y metaboliza los restos de sebo y proteínas, liberando compuestos volátiles responsables de ese olor tan característico. Hay una excepción. Aunque dejar la puerta abierta es el hábito más eficaz para frenar este ciclo, los especialistas apuntan a que si la lavadora está instalada en un sótano húmedo, un garaje cerrado o un cuarto de lavado sin ventilación, dejar la puerta abierta de par en par puede resultar ineficaz e incluso contraproducente si la humedad ambiental es más alta que la del propio tambor. Pero además, en ambientes muy secos, calurosos o expuestos al sol directo, mantener la goma completamente al aire durante meses sin usar el aparato puede acelerar su resequedad y agrietamiento a largo plazo. En esos escenarios basta con dejar la puerta simplemente entornada para permitir un mínimo intercambio de aire sin castigar el elastómero. La respuesta la tiene la microbiología fue publicada originalmente en Xataka por José A. Lizana .

noticias.contenido: Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle play the FTX founders behind ‘the greatest fraud ever committed’ in the US. It’s a mind-boggling story – just make sure you don’t miss a single moment What happens when you put really stupid clever people in charge of the world? Not as presidents (they currently trend mostly towards the merely stupid) or prime ministers (generally neither really stupid nor really clever), but in charge of the real world, which is to say the online world, the one that really governs us? We are watching that play out day by day, but if you have enough slack left in your dread-system, a cortisol spike yet to execute, why not add a warning from history to your consumption of horrors? Welcome to The Altruists, a breakneck breakdown of the brief career of Sam Bankman-Fried (played by Anthony Boyle) who, with his on-off girlfriend Caroline Ellison (played by Julia Garner), set up the cryptocurrency exchange FTX with the belief that it would revolutionise finance and – as the increasingly absurd/dishonest/knowingly satirical Silicon Valley mantra has it – make the world a better place. A very few years later, FTX – worth $36bn (£27bn) at its peak – collapsed and in 2023 the pair were convicted of various charges deriving from what the trial judge called “the greatest financial fraud ever perpetrated in this country”. Ellison was sentenced to two years in prison after testifying against Bankman-Fried. Bankman-Fried is serving 25 years and was ordered to forfeit $11bn (£8.3bn). He says he is innocent and is applying to the supreme court to review his conviction. Continue reading...

noticias.contenido: The actor’s latest roles see him go from a delivery guy on £40 a day to the notorious crypto scammer who stole more than $10bn. His sympathies are clear: ‘I wasn’t brought up to care about money,’ he says In the spring of 2019, Anthony Boyle went to see Cillian Murphy in Grief Is the Thing with Feathers at St Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. Afterwards, the 24-year-old actor hung around the stage door. “There were 500 people queueing up for Cillian, but I was the only one who wanted to meet Enda Walsh,” says Boyle, laughing. When the Dublin-born writer Walsh finally appeared, Boyle introduced himself. He was from west Belfast, he’d read Walsh’s plays at drama school, and it was his dream to work with him one day. He asked if Walsh would like to come and see him on Broadway, where he was playing Scorpius Malfoy, son of Draco, in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. How did he respond? Boyle grins. “He was sort of like: ‘Oh.’” Since Walsh never went to see The Cursed Child, Boyle assumed the writer had immediately forgotten about him. Then, a few years later, he received a letter from Walsh explaining that he was adapting Keiran Goddard’s 2024 novel I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning , about five close friends from a council estate in Birmingham who find themselves questioning everything about their precarious lives as they hit 30. He had scripted the part of Patrick, a politically outspoken graduate working as a zero-hours bike courier to support his young family, with Boyle in mind. Clio Barnard was on board to direct. noticias.contenido: Dice Raquel Elices en RTVE que Azuloscurocasinegro es "una tonalidad que nos recuerda que muchas veces nos equivocamos y, a veces, las cosas no son exactamente cómo las vemos". Habla, por supuesto, de la película de Daniel Sánchez Arévalo, que en 2006 contaba la historia de un joven que no podía escapar de sus problemas y responsabilidades familiares y de un amigo cuyo descubrimiento de cómo es realmente su padre le ayudaba a comprenderse a sí mismo. Quizás eso tiene algo de lo que busca Renfe con su cambio de imagen: comprenderse a sí mismo y recordar que, a veces, nos equivocamos. La compañía ferroviaria está inmersa en una renovación de su imagen . El pasado mes de septiembre, la compañía ya anunció que recuperaba su histórica galleta volviendo medio siglo atrás . Esa nueva seña de identidad, se apuntó, sería uno de los primeros pasos que se darían en su camino para redefinir su imagen. Ahora, el siguiente gran cambio apunta a cambiar la identidad visual de los trenes. Renfe quiere simplificar sus productos dotando de una imagen clarificadora del servicio que presta para cada tren. La nueva identidad la ha presentado Álvaro Fernández Heredia , quien era presidente de Renfe hasta hace unos días , posteando en la red social X la imagen que llevarán los próximos trenes . Raquel Ayllón, controladora ferroviaria y portavoz de SCF: "El CRC de Atocha tiene una cantidad de trabajo inhumana, no se podía ni ir al baño" Reimaginando en un momento complicado El cambio en la imagen de Renfe llega tras un trabajo intenso en la renovación de la identidad de la marca pero también en cambios más profundos que afectan a su funcionamiento en el día a día. Por ejemplo, la compañía ya tiene lista una nueva aplicación para la compra de billetes . Hasta el día 25 de enero convivirá con la actual pero a partir de entonces no quedaremos con esta nueva versión que, prometen, será más sencilla. Ese ejercicio de simplificación es el que se ha querido hacer con la identidad visual de los trenes. Éstos irán pintados en diferentes colores dependiendo del servicio que presten , quedando divididos de la siguiente manera: Alta velocidad: azul muy oscuro (casi negro) que se extenderá por todos los coches. Los trenes AVLO llevarán estas siglas en grandes dimensiones escritas en un azul más claro para contrastar y dejar claro que estamos ante el servicio "barato" de la alta velocidad. Por lo tanto, dejaremos de ver los AVLO morados como hasta ahora. Larga y media distancia: la larga y media distancia tendrá trenes morados que contrastarán con detalles naranjas. Cercanías: se combinará el blanco y el rojo compartiendo la mitad del peso en la carrocería del vehículo. En el lateral será más preponderante el rojo y en los extremos el blanco. Estos cambios en la imagen llegan en un momento complicado para la compañía , castigados en parte por todo el caos ferroviario que se está viviendo. Y es que aunque el trabajo para crear una nueva identidad visual no es, ni mucho menos, un ejercicio que se lleve a cabo de un día para otro, la noticia llega en momentos difíciles para el sector. Y es que el 2026 ha sido un año para olvidar . Probablemente estamos ante uno de los peores años (si no el peor) en la historia del ferrocarril español, con más de un centenar de fallecidos en la suma de dos accidentes que se producen con nueve meses de diferencia. En Xataka Adif invirtió 4.700 millones de euros en 2025 pero sólo 437 millones se dedicaron a mantener la alta velocidad El accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba) ya puso en duda cómo se estaba invirtiendo el dinero en el sector ferroviario español pero ha sido el de Urda (Toledo) el que ha hecho saltar por los aires la confianza que quedaba en el sistema, dejando al descubierto un amplio abanico de problemas que hay que atacar ( mantenimiento de las vías , falta de personal cualificado, presión excesiva sobre los controladores ...), que ha terminado con la dimisión de Óscar Puente como ministro de Transportes y la promesa de que se blindarán 19.000 millones de euros para que se lleven a cabo las reformas necesarias para devolver la confianza a los clientes. noticias.contenido: Los fármacos GLP-1 tienen muchas luces , pero también muchas sombras. Llevan años ayudando a pacientes con diabetes a controlar sus niveles de glucosa y desde hace un tiempo también están ayudando a algunas personas a perder peso. Esto último ha llegado a rozar la obsesión en algunas personas, por lo que se advierte a quienes recurren a estos fármacos sin realmente necesitarlos que pueden tener un amplio abanico de efectos secundarios. La mayoría son leves, pero dos reportes de caso publicados recientemente en una revista de psiquiatría nos recuerdan que, en pacientes con problemas previos de salud mental, se debe reforzar la atención. Ambos casos coinciden en que los pacientes dejaron de golpe un medicamento GLP-1 llamado tirzepatida y, poco después, desarrollaron síntomas psiquiátricos graves. Es cierto que tenían otros factores de riesgo y que, con solo dos casos, no podemos saber con seguridad si fue el medicamento el que causó el problema. Aun así, son una llamada de atención que nos recuerda la importancia de hacer un seguimiento aún más estricto en algunos pacientes receptores de los fármacos GLP-1. Varón, 61 años . El primer caso es el de un hombre que dejó la tirzepatida, conocida comercialmente como Mounjaro , en agosto de 2025. Comenzó a sentir náuseas, así que abandonó el fármaco de golpe. Dos meses después, se presentó en las urgencias psiquiátricas de un hospital con síntomas de confusión, paranoia, alucinaciones auditivas y visuales y empeoramiento de la depresión que ya padecía. Además, padecía un delirio de Cotard, que se da cuando los pacientes creen que están muertos o que les faltan algunas partes del cuerpo. Varón, 52 años . El otro paciente había abandonado de golpe el Mounjaro en septiembre, después de perder 45 kg en seis meses. Se presentó en urgencias en octubre con un episodio maníaco caracterizado por irritabilidad, impulsividad, grandiosidad y habla desorganizada. Si el otro paciente sufría de depresión, este lo hacía de ansiedad previa. Además, tenía los niveles de vitamina B12 muy bajos y consumía cannabis, una droga que puede aumentar el riesgo de padecer síntomas psiquiátricos. En Xataka Colombia Ozempic: la droga para la diabetes que se usa para bajar de peso preocupa a médicos... y cadenas de comida rápida Receptores en el cerebro . Los medicamentos GLP-1 imitan una hormona con el mismo nombre, cuyo papel es controlar los niveles de glucosa y reducir el apetito. Esto último es el motivo por el que suele usarse para perder peso. Por un lado, ralentiza el vaciado del estómago, por lo que la sensación de saciedad dura más tiempo. Por otro, reduce el hambre dirigiéndose directamente al cerebro. Esto último nos indica que en el cerebro hay receptores para GLP-1. Se ha visto que el medicamento puede atravesar la barrera hematoencefálica e introducirse en algunas regiones del cerebro. Una vez ahí no se sabe qué hace exactamente, pero podría aumentar el riesgo de ciertos síntomas psiquiátricos. Muy pocas personas. Antes de este estudio se habían publicado otros en los que señalan que los medicamentos GLP-1 pueden afectar a los niveles de dopamina. Esto puede ser útil para tratar las adicciones , pero también podría generar síntomas depresivos más o menos graves. En los peores casos, se han visto pacientes con ideaciones suicidas y autolesiones. Es cierto que estos casos psiquiátricos son muy poco frecuentes. Por ejemplo, en una base de datos europea se registraron 481 eventos psiquiátricos con semaglutida, liraglutida y tirzepatida, algo más del 1% de los informes. Los casos muy graves serían aún menos. No obstante, dada la gran gravedad que suponen, es importante estudiarlos a fondo para evitar males mayores. Si la mención al suicidio en este artículo te ha generado algún tipo de malestar o has tenido ese tipo de pensamientos, la línea 024 o la correspondiente en tu país te proporcionará ayuda 24 horas . noticias.contenido: World Anteater Day falls on Nov. 19, in recognition of the tube-nosed, ant- and termite-eating animals living across Central and South America. Closely related to sloths, anteaters generally live in trees. The largest species, the giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla), lives on the ground, though, where it rips open anthills and termite nests with its razor-sharp claws and slurps up the insects with its long, sticky tongue. The species is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List. Giant anteaters have disappeared from parts of their range due to habitat destruction and hunting, but habitat restoration and rewilding efforts are helping their return in some of their former range. A giant anteater’s return in Argentina offers a case for letting nature restore itself In 2025, a giant anteater returned to the Alma Guaraní reserve in Argentina’s Gran Chaco region for the first known time since 1986, reported Mongabay contributor Sean Mowbray. Habitat degradation in the Gran Chaco due to agricultural expansion and forest loss had reduced ant abundance by 30-50% compared to well-preserved areas, directly affecting the giant anteater. Alma Guaraní Natural Reserve, which covers approximately 6,400 hectares (about 15,800 acres), has been the site of volunteer-led restoration work for more than a decade. In some areas, volunteers actively planted native trees; in others, they used fences to allow the land to regenerate naturally, free from incursions by livestock, dogs, and hunting and fishing activity. noticias.titulo: Homo erectus teeth found in China’s rainforest topple theory of human evolution

El próximo viernes 28 de noviembre, la cadena de supermercados alemana venderá rebajado (a 149,99 euros frente a los 199,99 euros que suele costar) este Monsieur Cuisine Compact . Monsieur Cuisine compact SMCC 1100 A1 PVP en Lidl — 149,99 € El precio podría variar. Obtenemos comisión por estos enlaces Si no llegas a tiempo a conseguir este chollo de Lidl, Amazon tiene una alternativa que te puede interesar si estás buscando un pequeño electrodoméstico de este tipo. Se trata del Create Chefbot Compact Connect, un robot de cocina con 24 programas automáticos, 1.200 W y una capacidad de 3,5 litros. En el Black Friday anticipado de Amazon lo tienes disponible por 127,95 euros . CREATE/CHEFBOT COMPACT CONNECT/Robot de cocina inteligente multifunción Hoy en Amazon — 127,95 € El precio podría variar. Obtenemos comisión por estos enlaces Tamaño reducido pero sin renunciar a potencia A diferencia del Monsieur Cuisine Smart de gran formato, esta versión Compact apuesta por optimizar el espacio sobre la encimera manteniendo intactas las funciones clave que hacen tan prácticos a estos ayudantes de cocina. Con una potencia máxima de 1.100 W y un rango de temperatura regulable entre 37 y 130 grados, este robot de cocina permite desde sofreír y cocer a fuego lento hasta triturar o cocinar al vapor de forma sencilla, siendo ideal incluso para los que no saben nada de cocina. En Xataka Smart Home Lidl rebaja un 54%, en su Black Friday, esta tele MiniLED de 55 pulgadas con Google TV y Dolby Atmos Uno de sus detalles que llama la atención es la forma en la que resuelve la cocina guiada sin encarecer el dispositivo con una enorme pantalla integrada. Concretamente, incorpora una pantalla táctil LCD sencilla e intuitiva en el propio cuerpo, pero se conecta con el teléfono móvil para enviar directamente más de 400 recetas desde la app oficial al robot. Su jarra de acero inoxidable ofrece una capacidad de 2,5 litros , capacidad más que suficiente para preparar raciones diarias para parejas o familias pequeñas sin ocupar el volumen de un robot gigante. Además, incorpora una báscula integrada de precisión que pesa los ingredientes directamente dentro del vaso. En cuanto a funcionamiento, ofrece 10 velocidades, giro a la derecha (para picar y triturar) y giro a la izquierda (para remover alimentos delicados sin deshacerlos). ⚡ EN RESUMEN: oferta para robot de cocina monsieur cuisine compact ✅ LO MEJOR Precio de derribo (149,99 euros): ahorrar 50 euros en un robot multifunción con báscula integrada y cocina guiada lo sitúa en una relación calidad-precio difícil de igualar. Más de 400 recetas guiadas vía smartphone: aprovecha la pantalla del móvil para seguir los pasos y enviar los ajustes directamente al robot. ❌ LO PEOR Dependencia del móvil para las recetas... Aunque tiene pantalla táctil LCD para controlar tiempo, temperatura y velocidad manualmente, es imprescindible descargar la app en el smartphone para disfrutar de la cocina guiada. Capacidad más contenida (2,5 litros)... Si sueles cocinar por lotes grandes para familias numerosas o invitados, puede quedarse algo justo frente a las jarras de 3 o 4,5 litros de los modelos mayores. 💡 CÓMPRALO SI... Tienes una cocina pequeña o con poca encimera libre, vives solo, en pareja o en una familia de tres miembros, y quieres iniciarte en los robots de cocina con un modelo completo, fiable y por menos de 150 euros. ⛔ NO LO COMPRES SI... Buscas un robot con una gran pantalla integrada en el propio aparato para no depender del teléfono móvil mientras cocinas, o si necesitas preparar grandes cantidades de domida de una sola vez. noticias.contenido: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 19 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Original Annotated The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas Explanation: Today’s image could have been a painting. But what do these colors mean? The brightest star, left of the center, is blue Alnitak (the Girdle): a triple star system best known for being the easternmost star in Orion’s Belt . The instantly recognizable shape of a dark horse’s head at the center is the aptly named Horsehead Nebula . It is about five light-years tall and lies approximately 1,500 light-years away. It is made of dust and gas that obscure the red glow behind it, which is caused by hydrogen gas being ionized by the bright star Sigma Orionis at the top. The orange nebula with dark filaments on the left is the Flame Nebula . Closer to the Horsehead, the blue reflection nebula NGC 2023 is actively forming stars. The data for this “painting” were collected for almost six hours at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories , but the equipment was remotely controlled by the astrophotographer from his home, over 2,000 km away in Illinois . Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? Date November 19, 2026 Credit Mark E. noticias.titulo: El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama
noticias.resumen: Winter precipitation helped wake dormant seeds in northern Chile, carpeting the desert with what may be the region’s most extensive flowering of the satellite era.
noticias.contenido: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search September 14 October 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 14 October 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 14 October 24 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green, and white in austral spring 2026 following an unusually wet winter. The rain woke seeds lying dormant in the soil, setting off what scientists say may be the most extensive desierto florido , or “flowering desert,” of the satellite era. The rains came as El Niño was strengthening in the tropical Pacific. During an El Niño, the subtropical Pacific high that normally keeps the region dry weakens, while a blocking high tends to form in the South Pacific near the tip of South America. Together, these shifts push the Southern Hemisphere storm track equatorward. Beginning in mid-July, a series of storm fronts fed by an atmospheric river brought one of the heaviest July rain events in decades to a long stretch of Chile, from the Atacama region south to Los Lagos, according to Chile’s national weather service (Dirección Meteorológica de Chile). In August, back-to-back winter storms blanketed parts of the Atacama Desert in rare snow . The spring blooms that followed are visible in these satellite image pairs, which show the desert at different stages of flowering on September 14 (left) and on October 24 (right). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 acquired the September images, and the OLI on Landsat 9 acquired the October images. The pair above shows a part of the desert about 30 kilometers (20 miles) southwest of Copiapó, near the eastern sector of Desierto Florido National Park. The red-purple areas prominent in the October 24 scene are vast blooms of pata de guanaco, most likely Cistanthe longiscapa or another Cistanthe species, according to Roberto Chávez, a remote sensing scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Patches of red-purple Cistanthe are visible during a bloom in the Atacama Desert, shown in this photograph taken on October 24, 2026. Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Chávez and colleagues photographed the Cistanthe blooms (above) in the area that same day. They were in the field to study the bloom with satellite data, drones, and digital cameras. The project aims to use these data to map how the bloom’s biodiversity changes across space and over time, to inform land-use planners and conservation managers. The pair below shows another part of the blooming desert, about 50 kilometers (30 miles) southwest of Copiapó. It lies within a priority area of the desert cited for its biological significance, including the flowering landscape. september 14 october 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison september 14 october 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison september 14 october 24 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Cistanthe is abundant here in the October view, but the September scene (left) reveals another desert beauty. The green areas capped with white are blooms of suspiros, or Nolana , probably Nolana baccata , according to Andres Moreira-Muñoz, a scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso who studies plant geography. The researchers photographed the Nolana -covered hillsides below on September 24, 2026. White Nolana blankets a hillside in the Atacama Desert during a bloom, shown in this photograph taken on September 24, 2026. Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Satellite data have been key to understanding the Atacama’s blooms. A 2014 study used Landsat observations to map where flowering and fog-fed plants grow around the Copiapó dune field. And a 2019 study used NASA’s long-term vegetation record to identify 13 Atacama Desert blooms between 1981 and 2015. Compared with those past blooms, the 2026 event stands out. “This instance of the ‘blooming desert’ phenomenon appears to be the most significant to date—in terms of its extent, intensity, and duration,” Moreira-Muñoz said, “at least since we began using remote sensing.” NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey . Photos by Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile, acquired during Fondecyt Regular Project 1251184 (ANID, Chile): Spatiotemporal variation of Flowering Desert biodiversity via multispectral remote sensing. Story by Kathryn Hansen. noticias.titulo: Resistencia y barbarie, las dos caras de la guerra en una granja de Ucrania

Aunque no se ve nada, es capaz de seguir avanzando. Se dirige a una granja de cerdos arrasada casi por completo por las bombas en el distrito de Berislav, a orillas del río Dniéper, frontera entre los ejércitos ucranio y ruso . Conoce cada curva, cada bache, cada árbol. Circular a ciegas es la mejor manera de evadir los drones de las tropas del Kremlin. Seguir leyendo Diseño: Ana Fernández Desarrollo: Alejandro Gallardo

noticias.titulo: Ancient minerals reveal a missing chapter in Türkiye's mountain-building history

In southern Türkiye's Central Taurides, scientists have developed a method to date some of these ancient movements by examining tiny calcite deposits that formed as faults shifted. This new timeline alters the region's geological history. Researchers discovered a previously unrecognized period during which parts of the crust slid laterally, between the Early Eocene and Early Miocene. They also found that the region's later extension began around 25…
noticias.contenido: A mountain range can bear the marks of events from tens of millions of years ago. The challenge lies in determining when each mark was created. In southern Türkiye's Central Taurides, scientists have developed a method to date some of these ancient movements by examining tiny calcite deposits that formed as faults shifted. This new timeline alters the region's geological history. Researchers discovered a previously unrecognized period during which parts of the crust slid laterally, between the Early Eocene and Early Miocene. They also found that the region's later extension began around 25 million years ago, earlier than previously believed.

noticias.titulo: New mixing benchmark could help industry reduce energy use in stirred tanks
noticias.resumen: Solid–liquid mixing, where particles are dispersed in a liquid, is essential in many industrial processes such as slurry preparation, crystallization, precipitation, adsorption and dissolution. In such cases, effective mixing is critical for contact between particles and liquid, enabling mass transfer. Floating particles often pose a challenge in mixing because they are lighter than the liquid and tend to float at its surface. While impeller agitation does draw them into the liquid, the minimum mixing intensity needed for effective drawdown has been difficult to define.

noticias.contenido: Country: Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. IOM Yemen DTM continues to record displacement caused by the escalation in western Yemen. As of 17 November 2026, IOM Yemen DTM recorded an increase of 9,281 individual IDPs compared to the figure presented in the RDT report distributed on 16 November 2026, bringing displacement between 1 August and 17 November to approximately 356,602 individuals (59,426 households)1. This brings the cumulative number recorded since the escalation began in June 2026 to 357,658 individuals (59,602 households). The largest concentration of displaced people was reported in Ta’iz Governorate, hosting 145,344 individuals (41%), followed by Lahj Governorate with 95,580 individuals (27%), and Aden Governorate with 71,706 individuals (20%). Additional displacement was recorded in Abyan with 17,208 individuals (5%); Al Hodeidah with 8,244 individuals (2%)2; Shabwah with 6,183 individuals (2%); Ma’rib with 4,104 individuals (1%); Hadramawt with 3,576 individuals (1%); Al Maharah with 3,096 individuals (less than 1%); and Ad Dali’ with 2,617 individuals (less than 1%).

noticias.contenido: Countries: Ethiopia, Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, Uganda, Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. In Ethiopia, FM data is gathered in five of the country’s land crossborder points, namely: Dawele, Galafi, Metema, Moyale and Tog Wajale FMPs. In Kurmuk, data collection has been interrupted since 3 February 2026 due to insecurity in the border area. Between 1 and 30 June 2026, a total of 107,719 movements were identified across the assessed five FMPs in Ethiopia, highlighting continued population mobility along key migration routes. Outgoing movements (58,188 individuals) accounted for the largest share of observed flows (54.0%), whereas incoming movements (49,531 individuals) accounted for 46.0 per cent of observed flows. This indicates that more individuals exited the monitored areas compared to those that entered.

PRIORITY ACTIONS Sustain BVD preparedness as the DRC outbreak reaches 11,376 cases and 5,568 deaths (CFR 48.9%); maintain PoE screening (83,826 events over 14–16 Nov) and screen air arrivals at Juba International Airport. Strengthen cross-border surveillance on the Yei–Morobo–Kaya corridor given spread to Watsa (Haut-Uélé) and cases in Aru and Ariwara; sustain alert investigation and testing in Yei, Morobo and Yambio. Sustain cholera response in Fangak and Renk (Rubkona and Mayom have had no cases since 30 October) and investigate the Aweil West (Wedweil) cluster of 67 mostly untested cases; drive 100% RDT testing toward the earliest end-of-outbreak declaration (8 December). Deliver the Round 2 polio NIDs (17–20 November; 87% readiness) and sustain measles response; the Magwi reactive campaign is completed (12,953 under-fives), with Malakal and Canal/Pigi campaigns being planned. Investigate the six suspected human anthrax cases in Jur River (Western Bahr el Ghazal) and sustain Guinea worm surveillance (no human or animal case in 2026); maintain malaria response (48,675 cases, 47% below 2025).

noticias.contenido: Country: Yemen Sources: Health Cluster, World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. Key Highlights Casualties continue, with Marib and Lahj carrying the burden. The HEOC count reached 12,779 (10,519 injured, 2,260 deaths) by 16 November, +1,024 in eight days. The daily average fell to ~128 from ~225, but reporting was incomplete (58–92% a day, none for 9–10 November), so the figures are a minimum. Between 11 and 15 November, Marib reported 266 casualties and 49 deaths and Lahj 234 casualties; Al-Dhale’e still has no funded WHO-supported trauma deployment. The front line is moving towards Aden. Front lines moved rapidly through Lahj and are approaching Aden, which hosts the main referral hospitals, the Health Emergency Operations Centre and the warehouse supplying the response. Further movement may change casualty flows and displacement, disrupt referral and supply routes, and require WHO and partners to adapt their operations. Measles–rubella campaign reached 92.3% of target. MoPHP results show 883,896 children aged 6–59 months vaccinated and 741,713 given vitamin A (77.5%). Al-Mahrah (61%) and Socotra (78%) fell short and 73,300 children were not reached. WHO-supported teams vaccinated 6,007 displaced children in five IDP camps in Aden and Lahj. Displacement continues to be at about 3,150 households a week. IOM DTM has recorded 347,321 people displaced since 1 August, including 18,780 in the past week, of whom 55% went to Lahj and 30% went to Taiz. Cholera is falling in the five most-affected governorates, but a complex outbreak is growing in Tarim. Suspected cases fell from 638 (W40) to 321 (W45). Tarim (Hadramout Al-Wadi) has reported 172 cases of acute diarrhea since W43, 78 RDT-positive and 22 culture-confirmed, with both suspected food and water. A diarrhea treatment center is being set up. Fuel and medical supplies are critically short in Taiz. Severe shortages of fuel, surgical supplies and anesthesia medicines are disrupting emergency services, including operating theatres and oxygen generation for intensive care units, and hospitals cannot sustain the continuous pressure. WHO delivered 19.6 MT of medicines and supplies to three facilities, and IRY and FMF plan to support two city hospitals. Shortages are also reported across the front line. Health facilities in areas under the control of the de facto authorities are reported to be short of medical and surgical supplies. Alternative delivery routes and access negotiations are needed to reach hospitals on both sides. The trauma referral pathway has critical gaps. Only four of the 35 planned trauma stabilization points are funded, none of them in Aden or in the part of Lahj towards which the front line is moving, and referral dispatch is unfunded. Burn cases are rising, yet hospitals can offer little beyond initial stabilization and wound dressing. Mental health and psychosocial support and rehabilitation remain the weakest links, leaving patients without continuity of care. Funding remains the binding constraint. All 32 WHO-supported trauma deployments are funded only until January 2027. WHO’s third CERF request is being consolidated at US$2.4 million, including sites, mobile teams and supplies proposed by UNICEF and IOM.

noticias.autor: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
noticias.contenido: Country: Somalia Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Please refer to the attached file. Review Summary: Significant local rains in the south, little rain in the centre and north. During 10–16 November, Bualle recorded 159.9 mm, Balcad 115.0 mm and Awdheegle 88.4 mm, while most stations in Bay, Hiraan and the centre recorded little or no rain. In the north, Las Dacawo recorded 50.0 mm and Elafweyn 31.5 mm. Satellite estimates (IMERG, 11–17 November) indicate 30–55 mm over Lower Juba and parts of Middle Juba and Gedo. By 16 November, 37 stations, 33 of them with a Deyr normal above 15 mm, had already received their full Deyr normal, including Baidoa (405.5 mm, 176% of the Deyr normal), Galkacyo (253.5 mm, 390%), Awdheegle (265.2 mm, 169%) and Bualle (240.9 mm, 148%), which passed its normal this week. Borama (16%), Burao (21%), Luuq (25%) and Mogadishu (27%) remain far below normal. River levels are rising slightly on the upper Shabelle and the Juba but remain well below flood-risk levels. Belet Weyne rose from 2.90 m on 15 November to 3.76 m today, 2.74 m below its moderate flood-risk level. Jowhar (2.90 m) and Bulo Burti (2.30 m) are falling, and Dollow (2.86 m) and Luuq (2.78 m) are rising slowly. Flood water in Jowhar district is receding. Satellite images show about 55 km² of flood water in Jowhar district, down from about 87 km² last week. Radio Ergo callers (5–11 November) reported flash floods that drowned livestock at Garadag in Sanaag and a death in stagnant flood water in Hirshabelle, while many callers in the south and centre welcomed the rains and said they had not seen the floods mentioned in the alerts.
etiquetas: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

noticias.autor: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
noticias.contenido: Countries: Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Please refer to the attached file. Description of the Event Date of event 17-05-2026 What happened, where and when? Between 15 and 18 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared an outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) caused by the Bundibugyo strain as a major public health emergency. This declaration was rapidly echoed by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC). At that time, the outbreak mainly affected three provinces in the DRC, namely Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu. As of 18 June 2026, a total of 33 health zones had reported confirmed cases, distributed as follows: 21 out of 36 health zones (58.3%) in Ituri; 11 out of 34 health zones (32.4%) in North Kivu; 1 health zone in South Kivu. These figures confirmed that Ituri Province remained the epicentre of the outbreak. According to WHO data available on 18 June 2026, the DRC had recorded 896 confirmed EVD cases, including 208 deaths and 78 recoveries. Cross-border transmission had also been reported in Uganda, with 19 confirmed cases, including two deaths and seven recoveries. Although the Central African Republic (CAR) had not reported any confirmed EVD cases at that time, the country remained at high risk of disease importation due to its proximity to the affected areas of the DRC. This outbreak, the seventeenth recorded in the DRC and the second associated with the Bundibugyo strain, had progressively expanded towards provinces located near the CAR border, notably Haut-Uélé. Available epidemiological information indicated a high likelihood of ongoing undetected transmission in this province, which serves as an important population movement corridor towards the border provinces of Bas-Uélé and South Ubangi. Furthermore, several public health alerts had been reported in areas close to the CAR border, including: The report of a death associated with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever in Libenge Health Zone, South Ubangi Province, which hosts Central African refugees; A report dated 18 June 2026 from the Chief Medical Officer of Yakoma Health Zone regarding a suspected EVD case in a locality bordering Ouango-Gambo Health District in CAR. In this context, the combination of proximity to areas of probable transmission, intense cross-border population movements, repeated epidemiological alerts, and limited preparedness capacities fully justified the activation of a DREF preparedness operation. The operation aimed to anticipate and reduce the risk of EVD introduction and spread in CAR through proactive preparedness, community-based surveillance, and community engagement activities. However, the epidemiological situation evolved in a concerning manner, with the outbreak progressively spreading to provinces that share a direct border with CAR. In August 2026, Bas-Uélé Province, which borders CAR, reported its first confirmed EVD case in Buta Health Zone, becoming the sixth affected province in the DRC. The confirmed case was linked to travel from Haut-Uélé Province, highlighting the persistent risk associated with population movements between affected areas and border districts in CAR. As of 19 August 2026, the DRC had reported 5,208 confirmed cases and 2,476 deaths, compared to 896 cases and 208 deaths on 18 June 2026. In addition, 84 per cent of identified contacts were under follow-up. On the same date, another confirmed EVD case was reported in Viadana Health Zone, Bas-Uélé Province, in close proximity to the Haut-Mbomou, Mbomou, and Basse-Kotto health districts of the Central African Republic. The progression of the outbreak is particularly alarming. While three provinces and 33 health zones were affected as of 18 June 2026, the situation had expanded to six provinces and 55 affected health zones by 19 August 2026. This continued geographical expansion brought the outbreak significantly closer to the CAR border and substantially increased the risk of virus introduction into the country. Since the launch of the preparedness operation, sixty-four (64) suspected EVD cases have been reported and investigated in CAR. All laboratory test results returned negative for Ebola Virus Disease. By the end of October 2026, the regional situation had deteriorated further. Most DRC provinces bordering CAR were affected by EVD, including Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, South Ubangi, and North Ubangi. Geographical proximity, combined with the strong historical and family ties between communities living along the Ubangi River, facilitates significant formal and informal cross-border population movements. As of 25 October 2026, the epidemiological situation in the DRC reported: 10,060 cumulative cases; 4,887 deaths; 2,684 recoveries; 1,008 patients admitted to treatment centres; a case fatality rate of 48.6%; a contact tracing rate of 81.6%. These cases were distributed across eight provinces and 66 health zones or health districts. At the same time, the Central African Republic has progressively strengthened its preparedness capacity. The national preparedness level increased from 42 per cent at the beginning of the operation to 68 per cent during the latest assessment conducted at the end of August 2026. The 30-day acceleration plan validated in early October 2026 aims to raise this level to 95 per cent. As part of this acceleration plan, the Incident Management System has been decentralized to bring coordination closer to the highest-risk regions and their border health districts. Efforts are underway to make Ebola Treatment Centres fully operational in Obo, Bangassou, the Bimbo University Teaching Hospital, and PK24. Surveillance at points of entry has been reinforced, as have risk communication and community engagement activities, under the leadership of the Minister of Health. The Central African Red Cross (CRCA), which leads the Safe and Dignified Burials pillar, has trained fifteen teams of ten volunteers each to ensure adequate coverage of high-risk localities. Finally, on 22 and 23 October 2026, CAR and the DRC met in Bangui for a cross-border coordination meeting aimed at strengthening information sharing, exchanging experiences, and improving joint preparedness measures to prevent and control any potential spread of the outbreak in health districts on both sides of the border.

Despite global commitments to end all forms of violence against children, millions of children continue to experience violence across regions and income levels, revealing the persistent gap between commitment and reality. This brief presents the latest available global estimates on violent discipline by caregivers in the home and sexual violence in childhood, drawing on evidence from both development and…
noticias.contenido: Country: World Source: UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Violence against children remains one of the most widespread violations of children’s rights worldwide. Despite global commitments to end all forms of violence against children, millions of children continue to experience violence across regions and income levels, revealing the persistent gap between commitment and reality. This brief presents the latest available global estimates on violent discipline by caregivers in the home and sexual violence in childhood, drawing on evidence from both development and humanitarian contexts. The brief illustrates why accelerating progress towards SDG Target 16.2 remains an urgent priority and highlights the essential role of both universal and targeted prevention efforts and a strong, accessible social service workforce equipped with a package of evidence-based family support and child protection services. Accelerating progress will require renewed political commitment, sustained investment, stronger child protection systems capable of delivering evidence-based services at scale in cooperation with allied services such as health, education, and justice, and the large-scale implementation of proven universal and targeted prevention interventions.

noticias.contenido: Country: World Source: Save the Children · Nearly one in four children worldwide live in conflict zones, new report finds · Africa now accounts for 44% of children living near conflict worldwide, with an unprecedented two in five African children impacted · Verified incidents of denial of humanitarian access against children have increased almost 16-fold in a decade to almost one an hour AMMAN, 19 November 2026 – Almost one in four children worldwide are now living in conflict zones, the highest number since records began in 1990, according to a new Save the Children report. The figure represents an increase of more than 50% in a decade, jumping from 378 million in 2015 to 589 million in 2025, according to the report Stop the War on Children: Changing the Odds , which draws on data from the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO). The report found that the share of the world’s children living in conflict zones more than doubled from about 10% in the mid-1990s to 23.4% in 2025. Africa is home to the highest number of children living in conflict zones, accounting for about 260 million, or 44% of the global total. This is nearly a 20% increase from the 218 million children in Africa who lived in conflict zones in 2024. Across Africa, the proportion of children living in conflict zones more than tripled from about one in eight children in 2010 to about two in five in 2025, the highest level ever recorded for the continent. This puts Africa on par with the Middle East, where both regions now have two in five children living in conflict zones. Elsewhere, about one in four children (24.2%) in the Americas lived in conflict zones in 2025, one in seven (14.3%) in Asia, and nearly one in nine (10.6%) in Europe. The report also examined United Nations verified grave violations against children in armed conflict between 2005 and 2025, including killing and maiming, recruitment by armed forces or groups, sexual violence, abduction, attacks on schools and hospitals, and denial of humanitarian access. These numbers represent the tip of the iceberg for grave violations against children, as most attacks on children go unverified, said Save the Children. Killing and maiming accounted for the largest share of violations against children over the past two decades, with 171,712 cases verified since 2005. More than 70% of the cases were committed against children in five countries: the occupied Palestinian territory, Afghanistan, Somalia, Syria and Yemen. The report also found that the fastest-growing grave violation against children is the denial of humanitarian aid, with verified incidents skyrocketing from 509 in 2015 to 8,322 in 2025, more than a 16-fold increase in a decade. This amounts to almost one verified incident of denial of humanitarian aid every hour, on average, in 2025. More than 70% of all verified aid denial last year took place against Palestinian children. Denial of humanitarian access rose from just over 2% of all verified grave violations in 2015 to more than 21% in 2025, making it the second most frequently verified violation after killing and maiming. Rape and other forms of sexual violence against children are widely underreported. Even so, the report found that 28,909 cases have been verified since reporting began. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) accounts for 12,698, or almost 44% of the total, followed by Somalia with 4,534 and Chad with 2,979. Together, the three countries account for around 70% of all verified cases. In eastern DRC, 17-year-old Ana* experienced the devastating consequences of conflict after violence forced her family from their home. After months of displacement, they returned, only for armed men to break into their house, shoot Ana’s brother dead and rape her while other family members were assaulted. “We had fled the war, but it came knocking at our door again. [When the attackers came to our home] I screamed; I begged for mercy… but no one listened. My brother was killed before my eyes. I was raped,” Ana said. “[Afterwards] the hardest part wasn’t the pain. It was people’s mockery. They pointed fingers at me, as if I were to blame for what had been done to me.” The next morning, neighbours helped Ana reach a local health centre supported by Save the Children, where she received emergency medical care, including treatment to prevent pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, as well as ongoing psychosocial support. Gudrun Østby, Research Professor at PRIO, said: “We estimate that 589 million children were living close to armed conflict last year. These record-high figures are a stark reminder that conflict is devastating the daily lives, education, health and future prospects of hundreds of millions of children. Unless greater efforts are made to protect children in conflict settings, the consequences of today's wars will be felt for decades to come.” Inger Ashing, CEO of Save the Children International, said: “Almost one in four children around the world now lives in a conflict zone. What could be more important than their protection? The scale of this crisis is rapidly growing, and the systems meant to protect children are being pushed to breaking point. “We're seeing aid weaponised, attacked and deliberately disrupted. Humanitarian organisations are denied access, funding is being slashed, and needs are outpacing our ability to reach every child in crisis. Meanwhile, parties to conflict continue to disregard the rules of war, while new military technologies are changing how wars are fought, increasing the risk further for children in conflict settings. “Children’s rights and needs must be at the centre of decisions about war, peace and security. More than 20 years of monitoring violations have made the horrors children face visible and created opportunities to prevent further harm. This work must be protected, supported and translated into action. "Parties to conflict must uphold the rules of war, and those responsible for violations must be held to account. But ensuring the protection of children isn’t only the responsibility of those fighting. States, donors and companies with leverage over perpetrators must use it, through diplomatic and political pressure. To truly change the odds for children living in conflict zones, we must put their protection first and work towards the peace they deserve.” Save the Children is calling on parties to the conflict to uphold international humanitarian law, accounting for children’ distinct vulnerabilities, and to facilitate safe and unimpeded humanitarian relief to civilians. It is also urging governments to strengthen accountability for violations against children, implement international treaties and declarations that protect children and education in war zones, address the root causes of conflict and ensure children’s voices are heard in decisions affecting their futures. In 2025, Save the Children worked in 107 countries, reaching more than 58.2 million people, including 37.8 million children. The child rights organisation also responded to 113 humanitarian crises in 63 countries, supporting over 24 million people, including 13.6 million children. ENDS Notes to Editor: Read the full report here: https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/stop-the-war-on-children-changing-the-odds-2026 · The updated analysis on the number and share of children living in conflict zones is conducted by the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO). The core dataset used to map conflict patterns in this report is the Uppsala Conflict Data Program’s Georeferenced Event Data Set (UCDP GED) until 2025. To estimate the number of children living in conflict areas, and populations more generally, PRIO integrated the UCDP conflict data with population data from CIESIN’s Gridded Population of the World (GPW) and from the UN World Population Prospects. PRIO uses UCDP’s definition of armed conflict: ‘armed force used by an organized actor against another organized actor, or against civilians, resulting in at least 25 battle-related deaths in one calendar year’. A ‘conflict zone’ is defined as an area within 50km of where one or more conflict incidents take place in a given year, within the borders of a country. · The UN Security Council has identified six grave violations against children in situations of armed conflict: killing and maiming of children; recruitment or use of children by armed forces and groups; sexual violence against children; abduction of children; attacks against schools and hospitals; and denial of humanitarian access for children. These grave violations were defined on the basis of their egregious nature and their severe impact on children’s wellbeing. · Stop the War on Children

noticias.titulo: Atoms in sync: Superradiance offers a new kind of frequency comb
noticias.resumen: When scientists shine a laser beam into a crystal, they typically expect a steady glow as the crystal's atoms are energized and begin to emit light. But in early 2024, while searching for something else entirely, researchers in the lab of Caltech's Andrei Faraon saw a crystal flash in a regular rhythm, like a metronome keeping a beat. The flashes came from billions of atoms embedded in the crystal. Coupled to a tiny superconducting circuit, the atoms had become synchronized and started emitting light together through a special quantum phenomenon known as superradiance.

noticias.titulo: Reading the temperature fingerprints of electrocatalytic reactions
noticias.resumen: Electrocatalysis is key to turning renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals, and industrial electrolyzers typically operate at moderately elevated temperatures. Measuring how reaction rates change with temperature is also a powerful, yet underexplored, way to probe what controls them. Such measurements yield two quantities: an apparent activation enthalpy, reflecting the energetic cost of the reaction, and a prefactor, which is linked to the activation entropy.

noticias.resumen: Indigenous communities in Malaysian Borneo gathered on Nov. 4 to place a memorial stone in commemoration of their three-year battle with an oil palm plantation that threatened their native customary land rights and also endangered a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Placing the Ba Besanan Memorial Stone in the forest was partly a celebration by the […]
noticias.contenido: Indigenous communities in Malaysian Borneo gathered on Nov. 4 to place a memorial stone in commemoration of their three-year battle with an oil palm plantation that threatened their native customary land rights and also endangered a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Placing the Ba Besanan Memorial Stone in the forest was partly a celebration by the Berawan, Penan, and Tering peoples, but also a warning to current and future generations about the outside interests seeking to make money off their native customary land, one leader said. “I remind the people that we can’t overstate [the victory],” Willie Kajan, an Indigenous Tering member who represents the Berawan and Tering in Mulu, in the state of Sarawak, told Mongabay by phone. “We don’t know their next tactic.” Ukau Lupung, the representative of the Penan community at Bateu Bungan, places a stone on top of the Ba Besanan Memorial Stone as a symbolic gesture to mark its inauguration on Nov. 4, 2026 in the Mulu area of Malaysia’s Sarawak state. Image courtesy of Keruan. A surprise victory The Berawan, Penan and Tering peoples live both within and around the nearly 53,000-hectare (131,000-acre) Gunung Mulu National Park, and they rely on the land for their livelihoods and cultural preservation. Indigenous residents first detected logging there in 2018, when employees of Malaysian firm Radiant Lagoon Sdn. Bhd. began clearing land for development. Identifying these early changes could pave the way for timely interventions, enhancing future strategies for Alzheimer's prevention and treatment.

noticias.titulo: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
noticias.resumen: Ukraine's strike used homegrown tech while adapting battlefield lessons from its adversary.
noticias.contenido: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments

They are rare and important habitats for wild bees and other pollinators—yet how well they can support these valuable communities depends on how they are managed. An international research team, led by the University of Göttingen, has shown that long-term abandonment or intensive management threatens the diversity of wild bees. noticias.titulo: Who's to blame for a rogue AI? New legal framework maps accountability
noticias.resumen: Cyberattacks and other harms caused by artificial intelligence challenge the ability of laws to determine who is liable. Product liability law would point to the company that built the AI model, but AIs are trained on data the company didn't produce, and the legions of people who have used them also played a role. Free speech and social media immunity laws that treat an AI agent as responsible for its own actions could imply the AI agent deserves the same rights as a person.

noticias.titulo: El gobierno de Trump refuerza su vínculo con Delcy Rodríguez con un acuerdo militar
noticias.resumen: En una visita sorpresa, Pete Hegseth anunció en Caracas un acuerdo de entrenamiento conjunto e intercambio de inteligencia hacer frente a “amenazas comunes”
noticias.contenido: CARACAS.– Estados Unidos y Venezuela firmaron un acuerdo para ampliar la cooperación militar, un paso que formaliza el acercamiento entre ambos países tras la captura de Nicolás Maduro por fuerzas estadounidenses, en enero. El anuncio estuvo a cargo del secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth , durante una visita sorpresa a Caracas en la que se reunió con la presidenta encargada, Delcy Rodríguez . hegseth venezuela El entendimiento contempla entrenamiento conjunto, intercambio de inteligencia y otras áreas de cooperación militar . Rodríguez afirmó que permitirá reforzar la capacitación de la Fuerza Armada Nacional Bolivariana (FANB), mejorar su equipamiento y facilitar el acceso a nuevas tecnologías. Según la mandataria, la ayuda estadounidense servirá para hacer frente a “amenazas comunes”. Ninguno de los dos gobiernos ofreció detalles adicionales sobre el alcance del acuerdo. Hegseth dijo que espera profundizar la relación de defensa y la cooperación contra el contrabando de drogas. También elogió el trabajo conjunto con Rodríguez, que, según afirmó, permitió “estabilizar Venezuela y librarla de los narcoterroristas”, definición que el gobierno de Trump ha usado reiteradamente para Nicolás Maduro, el mandatario capturado en enero en una operación norteamericana y del que Delcy Rodríguez era la vicepresidenta. El secretario de Guerra -como le dice el gobierno norteamericano- definió el entendimiento como un restablecimiento de la asociación de defensa . Tras reunirse con Rodríguez en el palacio presidencial de Miraflores , visitó la embajada estadounidense. Más tarde, viajó a Colombia, uno de los aliados más estrechos de Washington en la región, que está plena ofensiva militar contra los grupos armados desde la llegada al poder en agosto del derechista Abelardo de la Espriella. Se espera que durante la visita Hegseth haga entrega a Colombia de un avión militar Hércules C-130, según el gobierno colombiano. Luego viajará a Ecuador, otro aliado en América Latina. El petróleo, detrás del acercamiento El acuerdo militar se suma al vínculo económico entre ambos países. Desde la salida de Maduro, funcionarios de Washington intervinieron en la definición del rumbo venezolano, con prioridad en la política energética y las inversiones. En agosto, North American Blue Energy Partners (Nabep) obtuvo acceso a largo plazo a 17 campos petroleros, que albergan cerca de una quinta parte de las reservas venezolanas . Como parte del acuerdo, Estados Unidos obtuvo una participación del 35% en la empresa matriz de Nabep. El controvertido empresario Alejandro Betancourt , controlador de la compañía y figura clave del acuerdo, estuvo el miércoles en Miraflores y en la embajada estadounidense. Dijo que conversó con Hegseth sobre la cooperación petrolera. Nabep prevé superar los 250.000 barriles diarios hacia fines de año, frente a los 224.000 que, según sus propios datos, producía a mediados de octubre. Betancourt es señalado por negocios opacos durante los gobiernos de Hugo Chávez (1999-2013) y Maduro (2013-2026). Según un informe publicado este mes, el gobierno de Trump sostiene que devolvió a Venezuela más de US$12.000 millones , casi el 99% de los ingresos por las ventas de petróleo venezolano a Estados Unidos, conforme al acuerdo energético con Rodríguez. Trump había dicho en agosto que Hegseth ayudó a negociar un entendimiento para que Washington tomara el control de parte de las reservas petroleras del país. Una transición sin fecha electoral La cooperación avanza en medio de la incertidumbre política . Rodríguez asumió el poder tras la captura de Maduro, pero todavía no hay fecha para nuevas elecciones. Aunque muchos venezolanos celebraron la salida del exmandatario, otros cuestionan que la Casa Blanca haya priorizado la reactivación petrolera por encima de medidas a favor de la democracia. La opositora María Corina Machado regresó recientemente al país. El secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio , dijo que su regreso fue resultado de “conversaciones de reconciliación” y describió el momento como la mejor oportunidad en tres décadas para lograr elecciones libres. El acercamiento coincide con una mayor presencia militar estadounidense en la región. El general Francis Donovan , jefe de las operaciones militares de Estados Unidos en América Latina, se reunió al menos dos veces este año con las autoridades interinas venezolanas. A la vez, fuerzas estadounidenses atacaron embarcaciones en el Caribe y el Pacífico que, según Washington, transportaban drogas. Al menos 240 personas murieron y las autoridades no divulgaron pruebas que respaldaran sus afirmaciones. Hegseth tenía previsto viajar ese miércoles a Colombia , donde entregaría equipo militar y trataría la cooperación en seguridad. Agencias AP y Reuters

noticias.titulo: NASA Sets Coverage for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Launch, Prelaunch
noticias.resumen: NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23. Filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus […]
noticias.contenido: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 mission launched Saturday, April 11, 2026, aboard the company’s Cygnus XL spacecraft atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: Northrop Grumman NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23. Filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is known as NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25. After arriving at the International Space Station, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, who are living and working aboard the space station, will use the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture the Cygnus XL on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Ground controllers then will install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Highlights of space station research and technology demonstrations being delivered aboard this Cygnus XL spacecraft include experiments to improve drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, predict cancer spread, and advance treatments for muscle loss, as well as improve radiation sensing and advance food production for future long-duration missions. The spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the orbiting laboratory until May 2027, then depart with several thousand pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, burning up harmlessly during re-entry. Northrop Grumman named the spacecraft the S.S. James “Jim” A. Lovell in honor of the former NASA astronaut. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Monday, Nov. 23 12 p.m.: Prelaunch teleconference will stream on NASA’s YouTube channel with the following participants: Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program Jennifer Buchli, chief scientist, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program Dave Schiller, vice president, civil space and sciences, Northrop Grumman Jared Metter, director, flight reliability, SpaceX To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 11 a.m., Nov. 23, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. The agency’s media credentialing policy is available online. Additional prelaunch updates will be available on NASA’s space station blog . Sunday, Nov. 29 10:25 a.m.: Launch coverage begins 10:47 a.m.: Launch Tuesday, Dec. 1 1:10 a.m.: Arrival coverage begins 2:35 a.m.: Capture NASA website launch coverage Launch day coverage of the mission will be available on the NASA website . Coverage will include live streaming and blog updates beginning no earlier than 10 a.m. on Nov. 29, as the countdown milestones occur. On-demand streaming video on NASA+ and photos of the launch will be available shortly after liftoff. For questions about countdown coverage, contact the NASA Kennedy Space Center newsroom at 321-867-2468. Follow countdown coverage on our International Space Station blog for updates. Attend launch virtually Members of the public can register to attend this launch virtually. NASA’s virtual guest program for this mission also includes curated launch resources, notifications about related opportunities or changes, and a stamp for the NASA virtual guest passport following launch. Watch, engage on social media Let people know you’re watching the mission on X, Facebook, and Instagram by following and tagging these accounts: X: @ NASA, @ NASAKennedy , @NASASpaceOps , @ Space_Station , @ ISS National Lab Facebook: NASA , NASAKennedy , ISS , ISS National Lab Instagram: @ NASA , @ NASAKennedy , @ ISS , @ ISSNationalLab Learn more about this commercial resupply services mission at: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-northrop-grumman-crs-25/ -end- Josh Finch / Jimi Russell Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1100 joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov / james.j.russell@nasa.gov Steven Siceloff Kennedy Space Center, Fla. 321-876-2468 steven.p.siceloff@nasa.gov Sandra Jones Johnson Space Center, Houston 281-483-5111 sandra.p.jones@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 18, 2026 Editor Jessica Taveau Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Commercial Resupply International Space Station (ISS) ISS Research Johnson Space Center Kennedy Space Center

noticias.contenido: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

noticias.contenido: Country: Malawi Source: World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. In August 2026, the World Food Programme (WFP), in collaboration with the Government of Malawi, activated Anticipatory Action (AA) in Mangochi, Nsanje and Zomba districts, following forecasts of drought conditions during the 2026/27 agricultural season. Malawi's reliance on rain-fed agriculture means rainfall deficit can quickly reduce harvests, incomes and food security. The activation follows a Ready, Set and Go approach based on pre-agreed drought triggers. The readiness trigger was reached in July 2026 and the activation trigger in August 2026 following consecutive forecasts of drought conditions, providing lead time to deliver support before impacts are fully met. The targeting approach combines food security information with drought-risk forecasts to prioritize support for households projected to face acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+) in the most affected areas. Assistance focuses on farming households with access to land and labour, recognizing that most vulnerable households retain productive capacity but struggle to achieve adequate harvests because of climatic shocks and resource constraints. To address the anticipated impacts, WFP is implementing the following anticipatory actions: Dissemination of early warning messages and climate advisories: Weather, agricultural, nutrition and hygiene messages will be disseminated through SMS, radio and community structures. Provision of agricultural inputs: Distribution of drought-tolerant and early-maturing seed varieties and fertilizer to 9,051 households ahead of planting in December. Distribution of anticipatory multipurpose cash assistance: Cash transfers of USD 130 will be distributed to the same households in January 2027 at peak lean season, helping them meet immediate needs while protecting productive investments. Unlike traditional Lean Season Response assistance, which primarily addresses food consumption gaps, AA aims to protect both food security and agricultural production. The 2026/27 activation builds on the successful 2025/26 AA intervention which was characterized by late onset of rainfall and midseason dry spells of more than 10 days, but not a severe drought. Compared with households receiving traditional Lean Season Response food assistance, AA beneficiaries achieved improved food security, reduced reliance on negative coping strategies and substantially higher agricultural production. In maize-growing districts, AA increased average maize harvests by approximately 1.2 metric tonnes per household. The intervention generated an estimated USD 569 in additional benefits per household, with every additional USD 1 invested generating USD 2.31 in benefits relative to the standard in-kind lean season assistance. The expected outcomes of this intervention are improved household food security; reduced negative coping strategies; protection of productive assets and livelihoods; higher agricultural production and harvests; and reduced future humanitarian needs. This anticipatory action activation is supported through USD 1.75 million in funding from Norway and USD 567,000 from Ireland.
